title: Efficient Fault-Tolerant Single Qubit Gate Approximation And Universal Quantum Computation Without Using The Solovay-Kit

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that the gate set "Z, S, CNOT plus the non-Clifford T gate" is universal. This is false: Z, S, and T are all diagonal in the computational basis, and CNOT merely permutes computational-basis states. This set cannot create superpositions from computational-basis inputs and therefore cannot approximate arbitrary single-qubit unitaries. A non-diagonal gate such as H is necessary. The later Introduction correctly includes H, creating an internal inconsistency.

The claimed general construction is not valid for an arbitrary self-orthogonal code as stated. Eq. (4) requires implementing physical gates P(alpha v_j), where v is obtained as a real-valued solution of Hv=w. In general the v_j are arbitrary real numbers, so these physical rotations are not members of the claimed recursively generated dyadic family P(pi ell/2^m). Thus the recursion cannot generally implement the physical gates required by Eq. (4). The special Steane-code example happens to yield integer coefficients (-1,1,0,0,0,0,1), but that does not establish the asserted result for a general Steane-like code.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, claim that arbitrary self-orthogonal CSS/"Steane-like" codes automatically implement S fault tolerantly
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The statement "Using Steane-like code, the logical Z, H, X, S and CNOT are automatically FT" is false for a general CSS code derived merely from a self-orthogonal binary code C. Transversal S requires additional divisibility/phase conditions, commonly a doubly-even condition on relevant X-type codewords (and conditions on logical representatives); self-orthogonality alone only implies even weights and does not suffice. The cited references cannot support the general claim as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Text preceding Method; asserted preparation and verification of |Theta(alpha)>_L
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proposed fault-tolerant preparation/verification of |Theta(alpha)>_L is circular. The paper proposes checking the non-Pauli stabilizer P(alpha)_L X_L P(-alpha)_L. Measuring this observable requires applying P(alpha)_L (or an equivalently difficult non-Clifford operation), which is precisely the operation the construction claims to synthesize. Saying that noisy preparation and stabilizer measurement produce high-fidelity states does not resolve this, because the required stabilizer measurement is itself not available from the stated Clifford operations.

The recursion depth is misstated. To obtain P(pi ell/2^m) from P(pi ell/4) by repeatedly doubling the angle requires m-2 recursive levels, not O(n) time independent of m. If each level uses a transversal operation on an n-qubit code block, the stated procedure has at least O(nm) gate operations (or O(m) logical recursive depth for fixed n), rather than the claimed "O(n) times through the recursion."

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusions, specification of m for the gate set
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The formula "m = ceil[epsilon / (log_2(1/epsilon) log_2 log_2(1/epsilon) ...)]" is mathematically incompatible with dyadic angle approximation. To approximate an angle within delta using pi ell/2^m, one needs m = O(log(1/delta)), e.g. m >= ceil(log_2(pi/delta)) up to constants. The paper's formula instead tends to zero as epsilon tends to zero (and normally gives m=1), leaving only extremely coarse rotations and making arbitrary-precision approximation impossible.

The abstract and Introduction claim a gate count O(log(1/epsilon) log log(1/epsilon) log log log(1/epsilon) ...), whereas the Conclusions state "O(epsilon log[1/epsilon] log log[1/epsilon] ...) gates." These are incompatible asymptotics. The latter tends to zero as epsilon tends to zero and therefore cannot be the number of gates required for higher precision.

predicted_errors.error_location: Conclusions, claim of a finite-set fault-tolerant compilation result
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The conclusion claims a finite-set gate-approximation result, but the stated collection {H, P(pi ell/2^m): m,ell in Z^+, ell<2^m} is infinite. If the intended set is truncated at an epsilon-dependent m, then it is not a fixed finite instruction set in the sense of the Nielsen--Chuang challenge and must itself contain newly assumed non-Clifford rotations. Moreover, the conclusion's appeal to analog hardware being able to "apply P(alpha) on each qubit" assumes the arbitrary rotations that the paper purports to construct fault tolerantly, rather than deriving them from a fixed FT gate set.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figures cited before Method and in Method
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text repeatedly relies on "Fig. 1" and "Fig. 2," including the alleged FT gate-teleportation circuit in Fig. 2, but no Figure 2 is present in the supplied paper. An unexplained "Figure 0" is inserted after Eq. (5), despite never being discussed. Consequently, the circuits essential to the claimed state preparation and teleportation cannot be inspected or verified from the paper.

The manuscript cites references [1] through [19], including references central to its Solovay--Kitaev, code, and fault-tolerance claims, but contains no bibliography or reference list. The citations therefore cannot be checked and do not identify the purported supporting works.
